payload.title: feat/one-subject-per-run at 7257753: one subject per cited run, a subject may name a base (step 4)
payload.body: Commit 7257753 on branch feat/one-subject-per-run, from 9429fc1. A Result keeps subjects, one {base, files} per cited command or sandbox record (R3a); a Hypothesis's subject may name a base, hyp subject --base, and a run at another base never covers it (R3b); an old Result's fingerprints read as one subject with no base (R3c); a subject naming a base is held only by a run at that base given exactly its files, so B plus a patch never covers bare B (R3d). Code and tests were written, and go test run, while building, before E's rule; the rule's checks run after it.

why: The step-4 candidate the /goal run builds for G-D1CH1R#3, checked again against #1, #2 and #4 to #8 on the same commit.
Step 4 builds on step 3; 7257753 holds 9429fc1 (step 3 merged) and adds one subject per cited run.

payload.body: Supports only if all hold, else contradicts. Each fails its tests on their assertion, and each diff is non-empty; a first attempt with empty diffs (quoting bug) is kept and not counted. (b) go vet and go test -count=1 pass at 7257753. refers.text: The owner's /goal prompt for step 4 says #9 is accepted, but the log holds no accept of it, and hyp admits an accept only of a referred limit. This run did not run #9's red-on-base pairs on 7257753 because the prompt aims it at #1 to #8 only.

why: Puts the owner's stated accept of #9 in the owner's hand so it can be recorded.

payload.observation: The fresh review of 7257753 against ADR 0020 and the lines gives six findings and one question, each recorded below as a limit; E-161WBK's rule outcome does not change. The reviewer also found line 1 byte-identical vs 33896ec on id-citation and recipe-base.
limits: F1: a sandbox record with two --patch Arms at base B is kept as one run subject {B, [pa, pb]}, so a Hypothesis tied to B plus Arm a's patch is never covered though that Arm ran at B; a subject has at most one patch.
F2: line 3's new tests fail to build on 9429fc1, so neither half fails on the commit before its change with a message naming its rule (line 9's case for line 3).
F3: no test runs rule 26 on a base: a bare-B subject re-tied after a run at B plus a patch must be admitted, and refused with 'subject ran in' after a run at exactly B.
F4: a Hypothesis tied with --base B and two paths of the same bytes is never held, because run files are unique by sha256 and subject files unique by path.
F5: hyp subject --base exits 2 when git is not on PATH; a missing tool is an environment problem, exit 3.
F6: replay admits a Result whose subjects are not empty while its evidence is empty, though subjects are copied only from cited records.
Q: a sandbox run at B with an --inputs file never covers a Hypothesis whose subject is bare B, because a based subject is held only by a run given exactly its files.

why: Records the fresh review's findings on 7257753 as limits of the latest Result.

refers.text: Its case is line G-D1CH1R#9's red-on-parent pair for line 3, and #9 is referred to the owner, who stated in the /goal prompt that #9 is accepted; this run's lines are #1 to #8.

Line #3 names only a patch; ADR 0020 says what is given over a base is a patch and input files, so a run at B with inputs is not bare B. Whether inputs should count is an owner choice of ADR meaning that no test within the Goal can decide.

why: Two review findings are outside this run's lines: one is #9's case, one is a meaning of ADR 0020 the owner decides.
